hero_section_description: A 60 GHz radar that clips onto your cane and warns you, through vibration, about what's above waist height. BIA filters the world and delivers only what matters
hero_image_description: This image shows an earlier BIA Radar prototype: a small, all-black module with a channel down the middle that rests on the shaft of the cane. The BIA RADAR logo is on the side, with the name written in Braille just below it. On top there are five raised buttons in a soft white material, each with a different shape so they can be told apart by touch. In front of the buttons sits a magnetic charging connector, and just past it a small dome that houses the radar, pointing in the direction you walk. The current version changes a few details: it has six buttons, charges with a standard USB cable, attaches to the cane with a wire ratchet you can tighten with one hand, and has an expansion port on the side.
objective_description: Walking shouldn't be an act of courage. BIA RADAR covers the space the traditional cane can't reach, bringing back the flow of movement
objective_item_1_description: While your cane covers the ground, BIA watches what's up high: branches, signs, car doors and scaffolding, above the waist, where the cane can't reach
objective_item_2_description: Don't wait for the impact to know there's danger. BIA vibrates ahead of time, stronger as the obstacle gets closer, and the vibration pattern tells you how high it is
objective_item_3_description: BIA follows the movement of your cane and predicts your path, so it warns you only about what's ahead and ignores what isn't a risk
objective_item_4_description: It works without internet, cell signal or an app, and the radar isn't affected by darkness or bright sunlight
objective_image_alt: 3D rendering of the BIA Radar attached to a traditional white cane.
objective_image_description: The BIA Radar fitted to an ordinary white-and-red cane. It clamps onto the handle, right near the bottom of it, so the user can still hold the cane the usual way, with the index finger stretched along the shaft. Sitting that close to where the cane pivots in the hand means you barely notice the extra weight, and the cane still swings and balances almost the same as before. The cane itself isn't changed at all: the same thin shaft, the same handle, the same red band above the tip. The whole point is that BIA works with the cane someone already has, instead of asking them to replace it.
expandible_platform_title: Inclusive by design, modular by necessity
expandible_platform_description: We believe you shouldn't have to adapt to the device, but the other way around. Our modular platform allows BIA to evolve with your needs, whether you're an urban explorer or someone seeking discreet support for everyday life. It's invisible technology that becomes indispensable

humanization_description: In a world of subscriptions and surveillance, we choose the path of ethics. BIA-RADAR is designed to serve you, not to collect your data or create financial dependencies
humanization_item_1_description: You purchase the product and it's yours. Period. No 'subscription for life' model because we believe autonomy should not have an expiration date
humanization_item_2_description: All AI processing is done locally on the device. Your location and your paths never leave your hands and never touch the cloud
humanization_item_3_title: IMPACTFUL AI, NOT JUST A BUZZWORD
humanization_item_3_description: Our AI is a tool for real impact, not a marketing gimmick. It filters what's relevant to you, reducing unnecessary alerts and ensuring that the technology serves your experience, not the other way around
audio_engine_description: Fully voiced menus and spoken instructions: BIA teaches you how to use it, so you never have to ask for help. On the Plus version, just say "Ok BIA" to find your cane when it falls or to move through the menu by voice. No complicated apps, no cloud

recognition_description: Born from ABDI's national innovation challenge and tested by blind users from the Instituto Paranaense de Cegos on a real city route, BIA-RADAR took first place. It's Brazilian technology built to restore what matters most: dignity
recognition_quote: We create new senses to restore autonomy and dignity

roadmap_item_1_description: It all started with a public challenge from ABDI: detect obstacles above waist level and warn the user safely. Existing solutions were too expensive and too complex for the Brazilian reality. Neosenti was founded to take on that challenge, and that's how BIA-RADAR began.
roadmap_item_2_description: Our proposal won the intermediate stage of the challenge. We built the first prototypes with a 60 GHz radar and started testing with blind users, guided by a simple principle: the technology should stay invisible and the experience should feel natural.
roadmap_item_3_description: After several iterations, BIA grew in ergonomics, precision and simplicity. At the final in Curitiba, blind users from the Instituto Paranaense de Cegos tested it on a real city route, with obstacles wrapped in foam, close to the worst case for a radar, and BIA-RADAR <u>won first place in ABDI's national challenge</u>.
roadmap_item_4_description: The challenge showed that different people need different things. BIA now comes in two versions that share the same board and the same mold: Base, focused on what's up high, and Plus, with a 3D map and voice commands. It also gained standard USB charging, a ratchet fastener and a single vibration motor. More than 30 blind people have taken part in development and testing so far.
roadmap_item_5_description: BIA goes to the lab. We start with a radio and electromagnetic compatibility pre-test, the first step toward certification. This is where instruments tell us whether BIA's radio stays within the rules.
roadmap_item_6_description: Our goal is to complete ANATEL certification, Brazil's telecom approval, in the first quarter of 2027, starting with the Base version. No radio device can be sold in Brazil without it, so this step comes before launch.
roadmap_item_7_description: Once certified, BIA-RADAR reaches the people who need it, and everyone on the waiting list gets special launch conditions. Next come the first expansion modules, which plug into the side port and let BIA adapt to different needs.
roadmap_item_8_description: Our journey doesn't end at launch. We will continue improving technology, support, and quality to deliver the best possible experience for our users. Because in the end, everything comes down to one goal:
